How much do real estate agents make in Flagler Beach?

There’s no salary. Agents earn a commission on each sale, so income scales with how much you sell. The math: each deal pays the sale price × the commission rate × your side of the deal (usually 50%) × your brokerage split. Multiply by the number of deals you close in a year and you have your gross. The calculator above assumes a 50% side; adjust the other numbers to your situation.

What moves the number most in Flagler Beach?

Two levers dominate: volume (more closings) and price point (higher-value markets). The Flagler County median, which covers Flagler Beach, is about $349,000, running slightly ahead of the Volusia County market next door. Flagler Beach’s oceanfront and barrier-island listings can carry a higher price point than mainland homes, lifting per-deal income for an agent who can find clients.

What the estimate doesn’t include

This is a gross figure. Out of it come brokerage fees, the marketing you pay for, MLS and board dues, and self-employment taxes. That’s exactly why a new agent’s real take-home depends so much on the brokerage: one that includes marketing and tools and helps you get clients faster can mean more closings and lower costs than a higher split where you fund everything. See how to become a real estate agent in Flagler Beach.

This estimator is a simplified gross projection and not a guarantee of income. It ignores fees, taxes, and market variation. Educational only, not financial advice.

faq.q: How much do real estate agents make in Flagler Beach?
faq.a: It varies widely because income is commission-based. As a rough estimate, multiply deals per year by average sale price, the commission rate, your side of the deal (usually 50%), and your brokerage split. At the ~$349,000 Flagler County median, 12 deals a year at 5% total, a 50% side, and a 70% split is about $73,000 gross before fees and taxes.

faq.q: Do real estate agents get a salary in Flagler Beach?
faq.a: No. Almost all Flagler Beach real estate agents are independent contractors paid by commission on each closed sale, not a salary. Income depends entirely on production.

faq.q: How can a new agent in Flagler Beach increase their first-year income?
faq.a: Close more deals, faster. That comes from training, lead and marketing support, and a recognized brand, which is why the brokerage you join matters more than the headline split in year one.
